Essentials 2.0 · Design research · 01-objectives-outcomes-requirements

Courses · Objectives / Outcomes / Requirements

Research for Essentials 2.0: Semester → Courses → Objectives / Outcomes / Requirements. How instructors define learner achievement and readiness, expose those expectations in the Learner Portal, and preserve links for later assessment. Competency setup, scenarios, sharing and Canvas delivery remain neighbouring modules. Evidence distinguishes observed controls from unverified behaviour.

Research synthesis · 27 references · 8 products

Curated from 39 merged candidates to 27 references across 8 products. The collection is below the 30–50 reference target because unrelated marketing, graphics and setup screens were removed. Functional evidence for instructors managing course expectations. Course products are the primary evidence; Asana is a labelled interaction analogue. Screens and sampled flow previews are historical captures, not live behaviour tests. Missing evidence is not a missing product feature. Q1–Q6 below retain the full reference board; counter-examples show meaningful contrasts rather than product defects.

What the best apps do differently

  • Udemy treats outcomes as explicit planning inputs with a minimum count and public destination; Teachable’s repeated checkout bullets serve optional presentation. Essentials should distinguish assessed outcomes from promotional summaries. Udemy · mobbin:3558619c-01e4-44de-9e1b-159104717ba1; Teachable · mobbin:007d841f-48d2-425f-bbaf-75ba21693a3c
  • Udemy authors prerequisite descriptions; Kajabi configures progression through a selected lesson; Codecademy states completion criteria; Skillshare exposes readiness information. These solve different course-management decisions and need different labels. Udemy · mobbin:4b041654-20d2-49dd-8779-2f45211103f7; Kajabi · mobbin:60f6d746-a953-49ba-9af9-784ff378d031; Codecademy · mobbin:6768ff06-2ec2-4e8b-8900-21500eb233a8; Skillshare · mobbin:84584675-5845-46cc-a5bf-90fafdd128b4
  • Udemy embeds an objective within a curriculum section. Asana instead offers an explicit attach/search/confirm relationship with progress roll-up. The latter interaction is transferable, but its completion metric is not evidence of learning. Udemy · mobbin:7fa8a407-5fc0-4de1-b169-0c7825495e47; Asana · mobbin:2f67fe8d-dbad-4ee4-ad75-5d08c69fe948
  • Udemy discloses that authored outcomes will be public, while Teachable’s preview exposes publication-state differences. A preview needs to explain what learners can currently see as well as how content is presented. Udemy · mobbin:3558619c-01e4-44de-9e1b-159104717ba1; Teachable · mobbin:e6757446-af84-43d5-bed0-da79c9a3826c
  • Kajabi lets instructors edit and accept or discard generated structure. Udemy constrains outcome input, and Asana prompts authors to define success. These are complementary controls; none of the captures proves AI can validate a measurable learning outcome. Kajabi · mobbin:4753100b-9870-45a7-88f7-447b3760e712; Udemy · mobbin:3558619c-01e4-44de-9e1b-159104717ba1; Asana · mobbin:2f67fe8d-dbad-4ee4-ad75-5d08c69fe948
  • Udemy visibly requires outcomes in early planning. Teachable’s sampled publication flow does not expose that step, so a publish flow alone cannot establish that outcomes are optional. Udemy · mobbin:3558619c-01e4-44de-9e1b-159104717ba1; Teachable · mobbin:ca328d45-4fee-42c1-925b-ff8e298dc4b8

Best practices top companies converge on

Recommendations inferred from the cited examples; these are design proposals for Essentials 2.0.

  • Use separate outcome items and state their learner-facing destination near the editor. Test order preservation explicitly; reorderability is not established by this board. Udemy · mobbin:3558619c-01e4-44de-9e1b-159104717ba1; Teachable · mobbin:007d841f-48d2-425f-bbaf-75ba21693a3c; Coursera · mobbin:2d300077-7580-47c6-875a-369da8b0a065
  • Give readiness guidance, progression rules and completion criteria separate names and controls. Use a concrete example in the requirement editor and show each enforced rule’s condition next to its configuration. Udemy · mobbin:3476c06a-c7b3-49ac-bc99-6875a0563ec6; Kajabi · mobbin:60f6d746-a953-49ba-9af9-784ff378d031; Codecademy · mobbin:6768ff06-2ec2-4e8b-8900-21500eb233a8; Skillshare · mobbin:84584675-5845-46cc-a5bf-90fafdd128b4
  • Keep authored outcomes near curriculum context and make downstream connections inspectable. Treat completion roll-ups and assessed mastery as separate design decisions. Udemy · mobbin:7fa8a407-5fc0-4de1-b169-0c7825495e47; Asana · mobbin:2f67fe8d-dbad-4ee4-ad75-5d08c69fe948
  • Pair AI assistance with editable output and a clear acceptance action. Combine that control with explicit success criteria rather than assuming generated text is assessment-ready. Kajabi · mobbin:4753100b-9870-45a7-88f7-447b3760e712; Asana · mobbin:2f67fe8d-dbad-4ee4-ad75-5d08c69fe948
  • Offer a learner preview that makes draft-versus-published state clear, and define the outcome publication requirement explicitly. Teachable · mobbin:e6757446-af84-43d5-bed0-da79c9a3826c; Teachable · mobbin:ca328d45-4fee-42c1-925b-ff8e298dc4b8; Udemy · mobbin:3558619c-01e4-44de-9e1b-159104717ba1

Open questions for Essentials 2.0

  • For simulation education, which readiness items are advice, which require learner acknowledgement, and which must block an event or scenario? How would a faculty override be represented? Kajabi provides a rule-configuration analogue; Skillshare provides the informational contrast. Kajabi · mobbin:60f6d746-a953-49ba-9af9-784ff378d031; Skillshare · mobbin:84584675-5845-46cc-a5bf-90fafdd128b4
  • Should course outcomes remain stable records with versioned wording when section objectives, scenarios or competencies change? Udemy’s local objective and Asana’s explicit relationship suggest different models; the competency and scenario sub-modules must resolve the seam. Udemy · mobbin:7fa8a407-5fc0-4de1-b169-0c7825495e47; Asana · mobbin:2f67fe8d-dbad-4ee4-ad75-5d08c69fe948
  • What demonstrates mastery: attendance, scenario completion, an assessment pass or faculty judgement? Codecademy’s stated completion threshold and Asana’s project progress are useful contrasts, not simulation assessment policy. Codecademy · mobbin:6768ff06-2ec2-4e8b-8900-21500eb233a8; Asana · mobbin:2f67fe8d-dbad-4ee4-ad75-5d08c69fe948
  • Must the Learner Portal preserve the exact outcome wording and order, and should instructors preview drafts or only the published version? Capture one same-course round trip before choosing the contract. Udemy · mobbin:3558619c-01e4-44de-9e1b-159104717ba1; Udemy · mobbin:04a7c094-adec-42d4-9f50-b4500ed8825d; Teachable · mobbin:e6757446-af84-43d5-bed0-da79c9a3826c
  • At the Canvas hand-off, which system owns outcome wording, stable identifiers, publication state and assessment links? This board shows local authoring and linkage patterns but does not supply evidence of Canvas interoperability. Resolve this in the adjacent hand-off module. Udemy · mobbin:7fa8a407-5fc0-4de1-b169-0c7825495e47; Asana · mobbin:2f67fe8d-dbad-4ee4-ad75-5d08c69fe948; Teachable · mobbin:ca328d45-4fee-42c1-925b-ff8e298dc4b8

Q1

Objectives are structured (list items, not free text) and reorderable

Udemy authors course outcomes as separate required fields with Add more and remaining-character counters (mobbin:3558619c-01e4-44de-9e1b-159104717ba1). Teachable uses repeated add/delete fields for optional checkout bullet points, an adjacent presentation pattern rather than a formal outcome model (mobbin:007d841f-48d2-425f-bbaf-75ba21693a3c). Neither capture demonstrates reordering. For Essentials, structured outcome items are well supported; moving items and preserving their order should be an explicit design decision, not a claimed industry finding.

Q2

Objectives are visible to the learner in the same shape the instructor authored them

Udemy explicitly tells instructors their Intended learners descriptions will appear publicly, and separate learner captures show outcome checklists (mobbin:3558619c-01e4-44de-9e1b-159104717ba1; mobbin:04a7c094-adec-42d4-9f50-b4500ed8825d). Coursera presents checked outcomes on desktop and module prose on mobile (mobbin:2d300077-7580-47c6-875a-369da8b0a065; mobbin:96fd5ba3-c8bd-4fbc-b875-9b58e616c622). These are not matched author/learner captures of the same course, so exact wording and order remain unverified. Teachable's sampled preview sequence shows that draft curriculum can exist in admin while the student view is empty (mobbin:e6757446-af84-43d5-bed0-da79c9a3826c). Essentials needs a preview that exposes both publication state and the actual learner result.

Q3

Requirements / prerequisites are enforced or only informational (and how that's communicated)

Udemy separates prerequisite descriptions into their own authoring field with a concrete readiness example, but no admission rule is shown (mobbin:4b041654-20d2-49dd-8779-2f45211103f7). Distinguish entry readiness, progression locks and completion rules. Kajabi configures a module lock against completion of a selected lesson and explains that an assessment must be passed (mobbin:60f6d746-a953-49ba-9af9-784ff378d031). Codecademy states all-content and 70% test-score requirements for completion (mobbin:6768ff06-2ec2-4e8b-8900-21500eb233a8); its runtime failure state was not tested. Skillshare communicates Beginner level and skills beside Watch Now (mobbin:84584675-5845-46cc-a5bf-90fafdd128b4), while Uxcel pairs beginner-friendly guidance with an enrollment path and a separate commercial upsell (mobbin:074a824b-a9f4-4e59-9039-fc5a59eb12c4). These last two captures do not demonstrate learning-prerequisite enforcement. A requirement description must not silently imply an access rule.

Q4

Objectives can be linked downstream (lesson, assessment, competency)

Udemy associates an objective with a curriculum section above nested content, but does not demonstrate reusable course-outcome links to individual assessments or competencies (mobbin:7fa8a407-5fc0-4de1-b169-0c7825495e47). Asana supplies the clearest generic relationship flow: no connected project → searchable picker → connected project with weight and progress (mobbin:2f67fe8d-dbad-4ee4-ad75-5d08c69fe948). Its automatic roll-up is an analogue, not evidence that project completion proves learning. Essentials should preserve a linkable objective identity while leaving competency setup and scenario mapping to their neighbouring modules.

Q5

Guidance for authoring (examples, verb prompts, character limits, AI suggestions)

Udemy makes authoring constraints visible: at least four outcomes and per-item remaining-character counters (mobbin:3558619c-01e4-44de-9e1b-159104717ba1). Udemy also supplies a prerequisite example explaining that prior programming experience is unnecessary; this is readiness-copy guidance, not a measurable-outcome example (mobbin:3476c06a-c7b3-49ac-bc99-6875a0563ec6). Asana asks authors how they will define success and offers AI improvement in its goal flow (mobbin:2f67fe8d-dbad-4ee4-ad75-5d08c69fe948); its separate onboarding screen explains choices and permits uncertainty (refero:195b0110-a6d4-404f-81bf-be74a9af62c1). Kajabi generates a course outline, then exposes editable results with Apply/Discard (mobbin:deee3b15-0748-485c-9921-7be6cc0a456a; mobbin:4753100b-9870-45a7-88f7-447b3760e712). That is useful review control, but no supplied example demonstrates action-verb coaching or AI checking whether a learning objective is measurable. Treat such support as an Essentials proposal, not observed convergence.

Q6

Where in the course-creation flow this step sits (required up front vs. optional later)

Udemy locates Intended learners first under Plan your course and explicitly requires at least four outcomes; the screenshot does not exercise the submission gate (mobbin:3558619c-01e4-44de-9e1b-159104717ba1). Teachable's sampled course flow proceeds from Setup guide through confirmation and launch success to Published, without exposing an objective step (mobbin:ca328d45-4fee-42c1-925b-ff8e298dc4b8). Kajabi's wizard shows generation and appearance stages, but does not locate outcome authoring. Those captures cannot establish that outcomes are optional. For Essentials, define the publication requirement separately from the order in which an instructor may draft the course.
